questions.q: What problem does a data contract solve, beyond what Lesson 39's schema drift detection already catches?
options: It makes an unannounced breaking change an explicit violation of an agreed specification, rather than just a surprise someone eventually notices after it happens
It automatically fixes a producer's breaking change without human involvement
It replaces the need for any schema at all
It only applies to batch pipelines, never streaming ones
questions.explain: Schema drift detection catches a change after the fact; a contract is the agreed specification that exists before it, making violations explicit.

questions.q: What does a data contract specify beyond structure (columns and types)?
options: Only the CI/CD pipeline's deployment schedule
Semantics — what a field actually means — and SLAs like freshness and availability
Nothing beyond what a schema test already checks
Only the Fabric Capacity SKU required to run the pipeline
questions.explain: These are the parts of an agreement a schema alone can't capture, but that a consumer still depends on being true.

questions.q: Why is enforcing a contract in CI better than just documenting it in a wiki?
options: CI enforcement replaces the need to write anything down at all
There's no real difference between the two approaches
Wiki documentation is always more reliable than automated checks
A wiki document gets stale the moment someone forgets to update it; a CI-enforced check blocks the build if a change violates it
questions.explain: This turns the contract from a promise people are supposed to remember into a promise the pipeline itself can't break silently.

questions.q: How does a data contract relate to Lesson 48's schema tests?
options: They are the exact same thing under two different names
Schema tests only apply to Databricks, contracts only apply to Fabric
Data contracts replace schema tests entirely
A schema test verifies a pipeline's own output against what it's supposed to produce; a data contract is the thing that defines what "supposed to" even means
questions.explain: The contract is agreed on by both producer and consumer ahead of time, and versioned for deliberate breaking changes.

questions.q: What makes a breaking change to a contracted field a "documented, negotiated event" rather than an accident?
options: Contracts prevent all schema changes permanently
Breaking changes are never actually possible once a contract exists
The consumer automatically adapts to any change without needing to know about it
Versioning the contract so a deliberate breaking change is agreed and tracked, instead of discovered downstream by surprise
questions.explain: This is exactly what Lesson 51 covers next — handling schema drift and breaking changes deliberately.
